issues.legal_issue: A pending proceeding concerning rights in land abates during consolidation when the dispute over a transfer’s validity can be adjudicated by the consolidation authorities as part of determining those rights.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed that the disputed plots had been acquired with joint family funds and that the vendor’s sale of the plaintiff’s claimed share was invalid, inoperative, and void.
The suit sought cancellation of the sale deed to the extent of the claimed share and possession of that share.
The defendants’ second appeal was pending when the area containing the plots was brought under consolidation operations.
The dispute over the claimed share and the alleged invalidity of the sale could be adjudicated by the consolidation authorities.
issues.conclusion: The suit abated, and the claims were left for decision by the consolidation authorities; the Court set aside the judgments below so that they would not impede that decision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5(2)(a) and (b) of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act, proceedings concerning declarations of rights or interests in land that can be decided in consolidation proceedings abate upon the required order, without prejudice to pursuing the dispute before the consolidation authorities. The substance of the claim, not its form, is decisive. A distinction applies between a document that is invalid and may be disregarded, whose effect the consolidation authorities can determine when deciding land rights, and one whose legal effect can be removed only by cancellation. Ram Adhar Singh v. Ramroop Singh & Ors. held that proceedings involving declaration of land rights may abate; Jagarnath Shukla v. Sita Ram Pande & Ors. supports adjudicating the validity of transfers in consolidation proceedings where that issue arises in determining rights or interests in land.

predicates.pending_land_rights_proceeding: A proceeding concerning rights or interests in land was pending when the relevant area came under consolidation operations.
predicates.consolidation_operations_cover_land: The land in dispute was within an area undergoing consolidation operations.
predicates.transfer_validity_is_part_of_land_rights: A party’s claimed rights in the land depended on whether a transfer was valid.
predicates.transfer_effect_can_be_adjudicated_witho: The effect of the disputed transfer could be determined as part of deciding the land rights, without first cancelling the document to remove its legal effect.

issues.definition: When a pending land-rights proceeding concerns land under consolidation and the transfer dispute can be resolved as part of determining those rights without cancellation, the proceeding abates.

issues.legal_issue: A respondent may support a judgment dismissing a suit on an alternative ground without separately appealing the rejection of an application raising that ground when the respondent obtained the dismissal sought.
material_facts: The High Court dismissed the plaintiff’s suit while also rejecting the defendants’ application based on the consolidation provisions.
The defendants had obtained the dismissal of the suit and did not separately appeal the rejection of their application.
In the plaintiff’s appeal, the defendants relied on the consolidation provisions as an alternative basis for maintaining the dismissal.
issues.conclusion: The defendants were not precluded from raising the preliminary objection in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A respondent who obtained the disposition sought may support the judgment on another available ground without separately appealing an order rejecting that ground, where there is no adverse judgment requiring an appeal and no res judicata against the respondent. The objection here arose under Sections 4 and 5 of the U.P. Consolidation of Holdings Act.

rule.if: appeal_against_dismissal and respondent_obtained_dismissal_sought and respondent_raises_alternative_ground and no_adverse_judgment_on_alternative_ground

predicates.appeal_against_dismissal: An appeal was brought against a judgment dismissing the claimant’s suit.
predicates.respondent_obtained_dismissal_sought: The respondent had obtained the dismissal of the suit in the judgment under appeal.
predicates.respondent_raises_alternative_ground: The respondent relied on another available ground to support that dismissal.
predicates.no_adverse_judgment_on_alternative_groun: The respondent faced no adverse judgment on the alternative ground that required a separate appeal.

issues.definition: A respondent who obtained dismissal of the suit may rely on an alternative ground in an appeal against that dismissal when no adverse judgment on that ground required a separate appeal.
